judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single numeric rule; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3-A.1's weight cap and the other bundle-schedule items.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise weight and count rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-A.1 caps bundles at 46 pounds, which this 42-pound-or-more band operates inside; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A reasonable number of bundles to facilitate efficient loading' is an open exception to an otherwise hard six-high limit, and the '87 to 46 pounds' figure is a corruption of 37.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 37–46 pound band ties to 3-A.1's 46-pound maximum, and the general six-high rule is contradicted by the black-and-white five-high schedule in the same paragraph unless read as an exception.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite forbearance as to an identified judgment and amount.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 3 preserves rights as to future incidents and 16-N's no-strike clause is the underlying obligation; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement that attorneys 'will develop a stipulation' — a procedural undertaking with no deadline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with paragraph 1's forbearance; nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Half recital ('because of the relationship which has developed'), half reservation of rights; the reservation is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its recital of the reason for the concession sits alongside the operative forbearance in paragraph 1, and 16-N supplies the underlying no-strike duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An identified sum and source; the OCR debris does not affect the operative terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the accompanying side letter promising no additional payments after six payments — though that letter and paragraph 1.A's installment schedule are hard to square.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise installment amount and start date; at $1,250 a month the stated principal would take over eleven years, which is odd but not ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The companion side letter says The News will require no additional payments once six payments are made, which would discharge the balance long before the schedule runs — a direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, complete waiver of interest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with paragraphs 1.A and 3; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Review the payment schedule, the Union's ability to pay and other relevant factors' obliges only a meeting, with no outcome specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It anticipates modification of 1.A's schedule, which the side letter effectively accomplishes by capping payments at six.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'More favorable terms or treatment ... with respect to the payment or disposition called for by an arbitration award or judicial decree' is a broad comparison with no method of comparison.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels 3-M's most-favoured-terms clause and the October 7 pension/welfare parity letter, three differently worded parity promises in one instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific, dated undertaking to withdraw an identified suit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with paragraphs 1 and 3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Provisions against strikes and disruptions of orderly relationships' is vague as an acceleration trigger, and the final sentence is garbled ('for any future violations of the aforesaid provisions to seek and obtain any and all other remedies').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-N's no-strike clause is narrower than 'disruptions of orderly relationships', and the side letter's promise of no additional payments after six payments cuts against acceleration of the balance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any major change in its operations which has an impact on a significant number of its NMDU employees' uses two undefined thresholds, with only an illustrative example.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-M.3 requires prior consent for any change in condition, a stricter rule than thirty days' notice, so the two mechanisms overlap uneasily.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It directs a named arbitrator to write a decision interpreting Section 16-M 'in accordance with his earlier oral opinion', incorporating two unrecorded external decisions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is direct evidence that 16-M's 'change in condition' language required construction, and it makes the meaning of an operative section depend on documents outside the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Every memorandum, letter agreement or side agreement shall be continued ... and deemed updated' is sweeping and 'deemed updated' has no ascertainable meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It revives side agreements that other provisions declare expired (21-B.4, 21-G.3) and collides with 21-D.VIII's supersession clause — a genuine whole-instrument incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'This Supplementary Agreement is within the terms of the current collective bargaining agreement' is an assertion of consistency rather than an operative term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several of its items (starting-time guarantees, manning minima) go beyond the main agreement, so the claim of being 'within the terms' is itself questionable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The arithmetic is stated but odd — two new situations of five nights and four days plus one night, 'and one additional shift (a total of 11 shifts)'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-A's Carlstadt floor-operations minimum and 21-D.III-style manning schedules address the same subject with different numbers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Including but not limited to' broadens assignments, while the last sentence makes log-jam clearing exclusive to the utility man — a general grant against a specific exclusivity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-A's control-room jurisdiction and 6-A.1's vesting of authority in the foreman both bear on who may be assigned this work.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Alco Men', 'regular floor work on the daily product' and 'provided all areas are properly manned' are undefined, and the reduction formula is stated loosely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves 'the obligation of The Times to hire from the shape in priority order in accordance with the Agreement' while itself fixing minimum hires, so it must be squared with 4-A.2's hiring sequence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is corrupted ('the nar..ed individuals', 'wir a job'), and it guarantees 'all regular situation holders' while then referring to 'named individuals' with no list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-J expressly contemplates starting-time changes on four days' notice and 20-E.7 gives the Publisher discretion over excess holders' starting times — both are cut across by this guarantee.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'At the required rate' is unspecified, though the trigger and the half-hour amount are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-L's travel-time provision covers analogous ground and was itself left to negotiation; 13-D fixes the overtime rate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-off delivery obligation fixed to the signing date; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The October 26 letter on posting job descriptions covers the same subject on a continuing basis; complementary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Concrete: a named vehicle type for two named employees' job.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-K requires the Publisher to furnish all delivery equipment; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As it does during the week' incorporates existing practice, but the obligation is otherwise concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-E.2(e)(1) already requires Albany runs to be driven through by unit employees; consistent and mutually reinforcing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple frequency commitment; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses DOT examinations; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such route shall be filed by in-shop bidding' contains an obvious error for 'filled', which goes to how the route is staffed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-B prescribes posting and filling of new situations generally, so 'in-shop bidding' here must be reconciled with that procedure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Including, but not limited to' opens the content of postings, and 'past practice' supplies the baseline; the closing disclaimer that the practices 'do not limit either party's rights' largely neutralises the promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-J requires furnishing starting times and days off to the chapel chairman, and the Supplementary Agreement requires job descriptions to the Chairman — three overlapping obligations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Whatever increase, however formulated' set against exceptions for productivity exchanges 'as determined to the Union's reasonable satisfaction' or amounts 'diverted from the negotiated pattern package' is highly indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps 21-F.3's News-specific pension parity clause and 3-M's most-favoured-terms clause, with materially different tests for the same kind of benefit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear holdover mechanism, though 'status quo arbitrator' is a label found nowhere in the operative text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-M.1 sets fixed annual terms for the Impartial Chairman and 16-G ends terms with the Agreement, both of which this holdover letter modifies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear holdover of the existing arbitrator list until a new one is selected and accepted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites 'the list of arbitrators provided by Section 16-E.1' when the list is created by 16-E.2, repeating the contract's own mis-citation, and it qualifies 16-E.2's sixty-day deadline.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise notice-triggered amendment right with a stated election.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It amends 2-N.1's monthly deduction rule, which is an express modification rather than a hidden conflict, though the two texts now say different things.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure statement of willingness to 'continue our discussions' with no obligation, deadline or subject-matter limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 17-D says the parties have bargained and settled all terms for the contract term, which sits against continuing pension discussions during the term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Only an agreement 'to discussion concerning the feasibility', with the substantive proposal conditioned on 'not involving the Times in increased costs'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 9-B contains the same cost-based escape for bulk deliveries, and 2-A/2-B unit coverage would otherwise bear on who transports the magazine.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If a sufficient number of employees are interested' and 'another acceptable bank' leave both the trigger and the counterparty undetermined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-N.1 and the Credit Union checkoff letter address payroll deductions, all consistent with this.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All other long runs' as a catch-all after named specifics (Long Island routes, news company runs) is a classic ejusdem generis point, and 'new vehicles' is undefined as to date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-H.1 requires heaters and defrosters in all motor vehicles within thirty days, a broader duty than this News-specific letter.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'When the six payments referred to in the Memorandum have been made ... The News will not, under any circumstances, require additional payments' is emphatic but the Memorandum does not refer to six payments.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly contradicts the Memorandum of Understanding's $1,250 monthly installments toward $177,844 and paragraph 3's acceleration on violation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The letter is reproduced out of order with its body split from the signature block, and 'the 48 inch height from the top of the skid' incorporates an unidentified award.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-D.VIII says the Newspoint agreement supersedes all other agreements and practices relating to Newspoint, which is hard to square with a promise to abide by all Newspoint written agreements and awards.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A deleted memorandum is nonetheless made applicable 'should there be a problem in the future arising thereunder' — self-contradictory on its face and dependent on a document not reproduced.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside the blanket continuation memorandum and 21-D.VIII's supersession clause, deepening the uncertainty about which side agreements are in force.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Medill Plan' is an unexplained proper name and the rules of eligibility are left to be posted rather than stated, so the letter fixes no substantive entitlement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-H and 13-I govern the joint Welfare and Pension Funds and 22-F/22-G the Times plans; where this plan fits among them is unexplained.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A reasonable period of time designated by the employee' and 'a written assignment satisfactory to the Publisher' are both open-ended conditions on the deduction right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-N.1 and 2-N.3 govern other payroll deductions with tighter mechanics; consistent but differently drawn.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Prohibits the subcontracting of bargaining unit deliveries except as it may exist pursuant to the contract' is circular — the exception refers back to the contract whose meaning is in issue.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-E freezes methods and extent of delivery, 3-F frees new routes, 12-A regulates wholesalers, and 2-E.2(h) permits other carriers; this 'clarification' does not resolve how those fit together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Continue its present practice' incorporates an unstated practice, while the annual statement obligation is concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-B addresses Times vacation checks and tax deductions and 13-I concerns Pension Fund shifts; the shift statement obligation complements 13-I.1 without conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Every obligation is conditioned on an unscheduled event ('when the planned DEC System is installed and operational'), leaving the timing wholly indefinite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The reference to shifts 'for which contributions were not made' presupposes credited shifts without contributions, which is in tension with 13-I.1's obligation to contribute for each shift worked in the unit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except if delayed because of an emergency or Act of God' is an open excuse attached to an otherwise precise deadline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-A.1 sets the first-year rates effective March 31, 1981 while the Agreement was executed in October 1981, so retroactivity is contemplated and consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A preamble reciting that a sub-committee 'discussed and agreed upon the following'; the mixture of discussion and agreement is itself uncertain as to what is binding.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is dated November 3, 1978 yet reproduced in the 1981–84 book, relying on the blanket continuation memorandum for force.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Recorded as a request and an advisement ('was advised that such vans would be ordered') rather than a promise, so whether it binds is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-K obliges the Publisher to furnish delivery equipment, but this item's status as an obligation depends on the ambiguous preamble.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Would explore the purchase and use of dehumidifiers' creates no enforceable duty and the concern is described rather than remedied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-H.1 imposes a substantive duty against undue hardship and hazard, which this item neither implements nor limits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Paid the same as the men in the New York plant for handling three-part inserts (500 or more)' is definite in comparator but silent on what the New York rate is.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-A's rate tables do not distinguish plants, so an equal-pay commitment between plants is either redundant or evidence of a practice outside the schedules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure statement of fact ('the Company indicated that new trucks had been ordered'), with no obligation created at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else turns on it; 3-K's equipment duty is unaffected.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sixers' is undefined trade shorthand and the measure is 'the same percentage as they are currently available', an unrecorded baseline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-D governs Newspoint conditions and its supersession clause (VIII) may or may not displace this November 1978 letter.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Five jobs would be defined when posted (Job Clarification)' promises definition without supplying it, and the jobs are named only by label.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-B governs posting of situations and the posting side letter governs job descriptions; this adds a third, vaguer obligation on the same subject.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement merely 'to meet and discuss', with no timing or outcome.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-L and 21-D.V deal with commercial and advertising matter substantively; this leaves that subject open despite them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A thirty-day meeting commitment about unspecified 'shop level problems'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16 already channels plant-level disputes; this adds an informal layer without conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same ambiguous 'discussed and agreed upon' preamble as its News counterpart, and the text is scrambled with the heading displaced.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Dated November 3, 1978 but carried into the 1981–84 book through the blanket continuation memorandum, whose effect is itself unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Concrete: two named jobs, one on each shift.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-A's control-room provision requires console personnel to be Journeymen and the Supplementary Agreement adds a utility man to relieve the console; complementary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific as to days, start time and bidding method.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-E.2 and 22-D govern over-the-road runs and transfer points, and Atlantic City lies outside the Metropolitan Area, so the run's terms depend on those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reviewed within a reasonable time' is softened but then capped at sixty days; the review has no stated outcome or standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Supplementary Agreement fixes combined floor hires at eighty-one including the 43rd Street plant, so a later open-ended manning review sits against that fixed number.
